memory_update.text: Add FARM as a high-relevance but speculative micro-cap candidate for private-label coffee and foodservice beverage solutions; survival depends on DSD execution, equipment-service economics, liquidity, and customer retention after the Northlake sale.
Add WEST as an underfollowed small-cap B2B coffee, tea, extracts, and beverage-solutions platform; next layer should test whether growth converts into margins and cash flow.
Add THS as a mid-cap private-label reference/discovery bridge because the Farmer Brothers Northlake acquisition created a clearer public-market mapping to private-label coffee manufacturing capacity.
Add JVA only as a speculative micro-cap shadow candidate; direct foodservice and private-label exposure appear relevant but must be proven material in filings.

For this node, the strongest chokepoint variables are not consumer brand awareness but customer qualification, roasting/extract capacity, direct-store delivery density, machine service, pass-through pricing, and working-capital resilience under volatile coffee costs.
Need a follow-up search for syrup, juice, tea concentrate, fountain beverage, cold brew, and beverage-equipment service providers that may not use coffee industry labels.

node: Private-label coffee, tea, extracts, syrups, and beverage solutions
summary: Expanded the universe around underfollowed B2B beverage suppliers tied to restaurants, hotels, convenience stores, institutional foodservice, and private-label retail channels. The strongest direct-node candidates are Farmer Brothers, Westrock Coffee, TreeHouse Foods, and Coffee Holding. The chokepoint is not branded consumer demand alone; it is operational execution across sourcing, roasting/extract capacity, direct-store delivery, foodservice customer qualification, equipment service, working capital, and customer retention. Farmer Brothers and Coffee Holding are micro-cap/speculative exceptions; TreeHouse and Westrock are more investable-size public mappings but require verification of segment purity, leverage, margins, and customer concentration.
